7. Renewal is a separate physical requirement

The candidate consumes substantial molecular machinery:

Stock	End state and treatment
Monomers and activators	Incorporated product, hydrolysis products or chemical waste
Protecting-group keys	Removed fragments in waste
Instruction clips	Severed and discarded
Program strands	Replaced during retargeting
Strip/unmask/trap strands	Spent duplexes; no recycling credit
Initiator arms and release linkers	Consumed during product recovery
Nicking enzyme	Conservatively charged as consumed
Scaffold and attachment chemistry	Claimed reusable only if functional restoration is measured
Flow equipment	Cleaned, calibrated and maintained

Replacing consumed program clips is allowed by your specification, but it is not renewal of those clips.

A proposed ready state requires fresh free initiators, correctly loaded blocked instructions, only the first selector exposed, defined buffer and temperature, and old-program carryover below a validated limit. Scaffold concentration or recovered mass cannot establish that state.

In the introduced ten-cycle aging model, a 0.3% loss of functional platform per cycle gives:

97.04% platform survival after ten cycles.
Worst available output declining from 1.163 to 1.119 nmol.
96.23% retention of first-cycle useful output.

Those are assigned lifetime sensitivities. At one hundred cycles, the same law gives only 74.05% functional survival.

For 95% survival over 600 potentially damaging events, functional loss must be no more than approximately
